title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Survey Plate Archive. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Survey Plate Archive
options.lineage: cartographic survey folios and plate archives
options.thesis: Every element is a surveyed specimen, plotted on a graticule and filed under a folio volume.
options.viewport: A folio rail on the left; the first plate fills the field — the orb plotted at dead center on coordinate lines, accession mark in the corner, props as marginalia along the plate edge.
options.risk: Reads decorative if the graticule is wallpaper instead of a working coordinate system.

raised.raise: Asymmetry as law — plates are sized to their element, never uniform cards.
Color lives only on hairline marks and the active plate edge.
Every plate carries a fixed corner accession mark — category plus number.
The copy button is a stamp press with a physical down-state.

options.label: The Specimen Cabinet
options.lineage: museum vitrines and natural-history accession labels
options.thesis: A public vitrine: each element pinned under glass with an accession label; copying checks the specimen out.
options.viewport: A title strip, then a cabinet grid of unequal cases — the orb centered in the largest vitrine, its label plate below.
options.risk: The familiar answer — 'collection in cases' is what most gallery builds ship.

options.label: The Live Specimen Sheet
options.thesis: A type-specimen sheet adapted to UI: prop sliders remap every live preview on the sheet at once.
options.viewport: The orb huge up top; below, a grid of all nine states breathing in step while a slider row remaps them live.
options.case: Fuses cleanly — props become axes and the orb's nine states become named instances — but it sits one step from the docs-page rut.
options.risk: Adjacent to every light-minimal dev-tool page; only the live remap saves it.

options.label: The Step-Row Console
options.thesis: An instrument panel where each element's states sit on a lit step row and a chase light shows the live one.
options.viewport: A tempo-style readout up top, one unbroken row of nine lit state keys under it — the orb panel below follows the chase.
options.case: The nine orb states map perfectly to a nine-key row; category browsing as pattern banks strains for arbitrary future components.
options.risk: Synth cosplay when an element has no enumerable states.

options.label: The Iridescent Edge
options.case: A pastel fringe on a white field never explains what a component is or does.
options.kept: Color confined to hairline marks while the field stays achromatic.

options.label: The Kiln Log
options.case: Staged firing states fight a browse-and-copy task; the soot field buries third-party component palettes.
options.kept: Asymmetry as compositional law — plates sized to their element.

options.label: The Collective Plate
options.case: A fixed cobalt-magenta-lemon palette clashes with third-party elements that bring their own color.
options.kept: The locked corner signature — every plate gets an accession mark.

options.label: The Road Case
options.case: Half-covered surfaces are the opposite of a legible component preview.
options.kept: The tactile press — the copy action stamps down and leaves a mark.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The Storybook-style docs layout every component gallery ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Left category sidebar, neutral canvas, tidy cards with copy buttons.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other component site by design.
